title_vi: ELK Stack: thu thập, xử lý, lưu và xem log

related.reason_vi: Chỉ mục tìm kiếm như Elasticsearch là một tầng bản sao trong bài các tầng bộ nhớ đệm.
Bài học Elasticsearch đi sâu vào thành phần lưu và tìm của ELK.

claims.claim_vi: Beats are lightweight data shippers installed on servers; they send operational data to Elasticsearch either directly or via Logstash. Filebeat tails and ships log files, Packetbeat sniffs network packets, Winlogbeat ships Windows Event logs.

claims.claim_vi: Logstash is a server-side data processing pipeline that ingests data from many sources simultaneously, transforms it and sends it to a stash, usually Elasticsearch.

claims.claim_vi: In Kafka's pull model a consumer slower than the producer simply falls behind and catches up when it can; log retention discards old data after a fixed period or size.

claims.claim_vi: By default Logstash buffers events in in-memory bounded queues, whose contents are lost when Logstash or its host is terminated abnormally. Persistent queues (queue.type: persisted) are disabled by default; they protect against loss on abnormal termination, but data may still be lost if an abnormal shutdown occurs before the checkpoint file has been committed.
claims.section: Memory queue; persistent-queues.md: Limitations of persistent queues, Configuring persistent queues

claims.claim_vi: The Logstash Kafka input's enable_auto_commit defaults to true: it periodically commits to Kafka the offsets of messages already returned by the consumer, and the committed offset is where consumption resumes when the process fails (auto_commit_interval_ms default 5000).

claims.claim_vi: ELK is Elasticsearch, Logstash and Kibana; Beats was developed later as lightweight agents; four-step workflow Beats, Logstash, Elasticsearch, Kibana, with an optional Kafka queue.

design_notes_vi: Ba khung: bốn bước theo thứ tự dữ liệu đi, một khung riêng cho Kafka làm vùng đệm, và ba điều cần nhớ. Bỏ con số và lời khen về giá. Không dùng ảnh nguồn.
source_deviations: Source draws Beats to Logstash as fixed; the lesson adds, from the Beats README, that Beats can send directly to Elasticsearch and Logstash is optional.
Source says Kafka decouples producers and consumers; the lesson explains why from Kafka's design document (pull model, retention).

Kafka's retention is scoped to records Logstash has not read: with the default auto-commit and in-memory queue, an abnormal Logstash termination loses the in-flight records; the persistent queue (off by default) reduces that (Logstash docs).
Source's claim that ELK is popular for a reasonable price is dropped: no source to check it.
